title: World War II: Key Events & Turning Points
description: The major battles, invasions, and conferences of World War II, with when each happened and why it mattered.
subject: history

cards.definition: Germany invaded Poland on September 1, 1939; Britain and France declared war on Germany two days later, starting the war in Europe.
Japan's surprise attack on the U.S. Pacific Fleet in Hawaii on December 7, 1941; the United States declared war on Japan the next day.
June 6, 1944 Allied amphibious landings on the beaches of Normandy, France, opening a western front against Germany as part of Operation Overlord.
August 1939 nonaggression pact between Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union, with secret protocols dividing Eastern Europe between them.
Late May to early June 1940 rescue of more than 300,000 Allied troops from the beaches of Dunkirk, France, as German forces closed in.
France signed an armistice with Germany in June 1940 after a rapid German offensive, leaving Britain to fight on without its main ally on the continent.
1940 air campaign in which the Royal Air Force defeated the Luftwaffe's bid for air superiority over Britain, forcing Germany to shelve its invasion plans.
Sustained German bombing of British cities, especially London, from September 1940 to May 1941.
March 1941 U.S. law letting the president supply war materials to Allied nations such as Britain, before the United States entered the war.
Germany's invasion of the Soviet Union, launched June 22, 1941, which opened the Eastern Front, the war's largest theater of land combat.
June 1942 naval battle in which the U.S. sank four Japanese aircraft carriers, turning the tide of the war in the Pacific.
August 1942 to February 1943 fight for Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands; the first major Allied land offensive against Japan.
Late 1942 British-led victory in Egypt that drove back Axis forces and marked a turning point in the North African campaign.
November 1942 Anglo-American landings in French North Africa, in Morocco and Algeria.
August 1942 to February 1943 battle that ended with the surrender of the German Sixth Army; widely seen as the turning point on the Eastern Front.
July 1943 battle in the Soviet Union, one of the largest tank battles in history; afterward the Soviets held the strategic initiative in the East.
July 1943 Allied landings in Sicily that helped bring about Mussolini's removal from power later that month.
October 1944 naval battle in the Philippines, often called the largest naval battle in history, which crippled the Japanese fleet.
Germany's last major offensive in the West, launched through the Ardennes in December 1944 and defeated by January 1945.
February 1945 meeting of Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin to plan the defeat of Germany and the shape of postwar Europe.
May 8, 1945, when the Allies celebrated Germany's unconditional surrender, ending the war in Europe.

cards.term: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
cards.definition: The U.S. dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima on August 6, 1945, and Nagasaki on August 9, 1945, the only use of nuclear weapons in war.
Victory over Japan. Japan announced its surrender on August 15, 1945, and signed the formal surrender on September 2, 1945, ending World War II.
